title: Parvah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Middot 5:3 mentions “the Chamber of Parvah.” Hyman summarizes Maimonides as saying that Parvah was the name of an idolater who dug through the wall to watch the priest perform the service and was killed there. He gives Bartenura’s explanation of Parvah as a sorcerer and cites the Rash for the view that it is not a person’s name.

notes.text: The commentator cited as הר״ש is not securely identified here. The explanations of a slain tunnel-digger, a sorcerer and a nonpersonal term remain separate.

The saved whole Vilna RambamMiddot5:3 scalar calls Parvah an amgushi who tunnelled to watch the service and was killed; whole Torat-Emet Bartenura gives the sorcerer account and quotes Rambam. These corroborate Hyman’s reported explanations, not a historical finding about a person. Hyman’s idolater wording and the named amgushi designation remain distinct. The failed RabbeinuShemaya title fetch is not proof that no commentary exists; it remains a candidate for הר״ש, not an admitted expansion. No secure Shimshon-of-Sens identification or nonpersonal etymology is newly adopted.

Maimonides uses the word amgushi for the person who tunneled through the wall. Bartenura says that the named sorcerer built the chamber by magic, then separately cites Maimonides’ tunneling account. Tosafot Yom Tov quotes הרר״ש for a different explanation: the chamber was named for the oxhides salted there, while the sorcerer Parvah built the bath above it. The exact expansion of Hyman’s siglum remains uncertain.
